::: {#def-perplexity}

#### Perplexity

The **perplexity** of a [language model](#def-language-model) on a sequence $x_1, \dots, x_n$ is

$$
\expf{-\avgtof{t}{n}{\logf{\condPr{X_t = x_t}{x_1, \dots, x_{t-1}}}}},
$$

the exponential of the average negative log probability per symbol
[@jurafsky2026slp, section 3.3].
It equals the probability of the whole sequence raised to the power $-1/n$,
and it is the same number
when the logs are base 2 and the exponential is $2^{(\cdot)}$.
The DATA 471 notes define it for any classifier in [the same way](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#eq-perplexity),
and find that a model
which gives probability $1/K$ to each of $K$ symbols has perplexity $K$.
Lower is better.

:::
